decisions.statement: An initiative is named by the slug the initiative declares.
An intent is named by the statement that intent states rather than by its place.
The place the intent is moved onto is named by the intent already holding that place.
Both places are read off the page as the change lands rather than named here.
The intent moved takes the place the intent moved onto holds.
An intent moved onto a higher intent sits before that intent.
An intent moved onto a lower intent sits after that intent.
A name that is no initiative is refused.
A call naming other than three words is refused.
A statement of no text is refused whichever intent that statement names.
An intent moved onto itself is refused.
A statement no intent of that initiative states is refused by the change rather than here.
An intent moved onto an intent the page no longer states is refused rather than placed.
Carrying the intent is left to the mechanical change with one value.
A run says the commit that run landed.
Every answer here is built by a function rather than written out as a value.
A change that refused is a fault of the data.
Nothing here writes a body.
No check runs over the change a run lands.
A run that wrote before it threw says in its refusal what that run had written.
A fault carries the code that fault names and says where it was thrown.

definition: the command carrying one intent onto the place another intent of its initiative holds
